blocks.txt: This book really does not need an introduction. All I want to say to anyone caring enough to be reading this is - ENJOY!

A word about the recipes contained herein:  This is by no means meant to be a complete cookbook or even an instructive cookbook. What I hope to do is record, primarily for Dré, recipes I hope don't get lost. Some of the recipes are handed down from another generation, some are passed on from friends, some are adulterated from cookbooks or newspapers and some are originals. I don't intend to distinguish with any consistency.

You will also notice that the formats are inconsistent. This I chose to do, in some cases because I liked one format more than another, or to my mind it made the recipe easier to use and in other cases, because it preserved the original.

1 - Glass - Usually means a juice glass ( approx 5 ozs.)
2 - Oven temperatures unless specified are usually 350.

3 - Where no directions are given it is because Grandma said "All cakes are baked the same way!" That is to say, first cream fat with sugar, add eggs (usually on at a time), then add flour and liquids alternately starting and ending with flour.
4 - Quantities yielded aren't given either but you can be rest assured they are large.

5 - *To the best of my recollection I have, at some time or another, eaten most of these things. I'll star those that I thought were, or remember to be, outstanding. Also more of Grandma's recipes can be found in the other sections.*
6 - If you have any questions you can call me.

For shortbread:  Blend blue cheese and butter in processor until creamy.  Add flour, cornstarch, salt and pepper. Using on/off turns, process until mixture resembles coarse meal. OPEN FLAME:  Wash and dry vegetable to be roasted, most commonly eggplants or peppers.  Lightly rub vegetable with oil to aid in charring. The vegetable is now ready to be used.  At this point, you can slice it or chop it, or in the case of eggplant, mash it.  Then you can dress it or not as called for in any recipe.

title: STINCO DI VITELLA AGLI ODORI  VEAL SHANK IN VEGETABLE SAUCE SERVES 4 OR 8

blocks.txt: I first had veal shanks prepared this way (whole) at a cooking class given by G. Bugialli in Pittsburgh on 4/13/97.  At the time I thought they were great. 1 or 2 veal shanks, each about 2 pounds with the bone
For the sauce: (see note below)
3 stalks celery

1 red onion, chopped
15 sprigs Italian parsley, leaves only
6 large fresh basil leaves
4 Tbsp olive oil
½ C unbleached all-purpose flour
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
1 C dry white wine
2 C chicken or vegetable broth, preferably homemade
1 - Tie the veal shank or shanks.
2 - Coarsely chop celery, carrots, garlic, parsley and basil  together.

3 - Preheat the oven to 400º, then place a heavy casserole with the oil over medium heat and when the oil is warm, lightly flour the shank/s and place in the casserole.  Sauté them all over for 10 minutes or until golden on all sides.  Season the meat with salt and pepper.  Pour in the wine and let evaporate for 5 minutes. (This could be made before frying pork.  Keep hot.)

items: 3 large onions (2½ lbs) halved and sliced ½" thick
3 med cloves garlic, minced or pressed ( 1Tbsp)

blocks.txt: 1 - Adjust oven rack to lower-middle position; heat oven to 300º.  Line 13x9" baking dish with two 24" long sheets of 18" wide heavy-duty foil, laying sheets perpendicular to each other and allowing excess foil to extend beyond edges of pan.  Pat brisket dry with paper towels.  Place brisket fat side up on cutting board; using fork, poke holes in meat through fat layer about 1 inch apart.  Season both sides of brisket liberally with salt and pepper.

2 - Heat 1 tsp oil in 12" skillet over medium-high heat until oil just begins to smoke.  Place brisket fat side up in skillet (brisket may climb up sides of skillet); weight brisket with heavy Dutch oven or cast-iron skillet and cook until well browned, about 7 minutes.  Remove weight; using tongs, flip brisket and cook on second side without weight until well browned, about 7 minutes longer.  Transfer brisket to platter.

3 - Pour off all but 1 Tbsp fat from pan (or, if not enough, add enough oil to equal 1 tablespoon); stir in onions, sugar, and ½ tsp salt and cook over medium-high heat, stirring occasionally, until onions are softened and golden, 10-12 minutes.  Add garlic and cook, stirring frequently, until fragrant, about 1 minute; add tomato paste and cook, stirring to combine, until paste darkens, about 2 minutes.  Add paprika and cayenne and cook, stirring constantly, until fragrant, about 1 minute. Sprinkle flour over onions and cook, stirring constantly, until well combined, about 2 minutes.  Add broth, wine, bay, and thyme, stirring to scrape up browned bits from pan.  Bring to simmer and simmer about 5 minutes to fully thicken.

4 - Pour sauce and onions into foil-lined baking dish. Nestle brisket, fat side up, in sauce and onions.  Fold foil extensions over and seal . Place in oven and cook until fork can be inserted into and removed from center of brisket easily, 3½-4 hours (when testing for doneness, open foil carefully as contents will be steaming).  When done carefully open foil and let brisket cool at room temperature for 20-30 minutes.

5 - Transfer brisket to large bowl; set strainer over bowl and strain sauce over brisket. Discard bay and thyme from onions and transfer onions to small bowl.  Cover both bowls, cut vents in plastic with paring knife, and refrigerate overnight.

6 - About 45 minutes before serving, adjust oven rack to lower-middle position; heat oven to 350º.  While oven heats, transfer cold brisket to cutting board.  Scrape off and discard any congealed fat from sauce, then transfer sauce to medium saucepan and heat over medium heat until warm, skimming any fat on surface (you should have about 2 cups sauce without onions; if no, simmeron  medium-high heat until reduced to 2 cups).  While sauce heats, slice brisket against grain into ¼" thick slices, trimming any excess fat. Place slices back in 13x9" baking dish. Stir reserved onions and vinegar into warmed sauce and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.  Pour sauce over brisket slices, cover baking dish with foil, and bake until heated through, 25 to 30 minutes. Serve immediately.

To Make and Serve the Brisket on the Same Day
If you would like to make and serve the brisket on the same day, after removing the brisket from the oven in step 4, reseal the foil and let the brisket stand at room temperature for an hour. Then transfer the brisket to a cutting board and continue with the recipe to strain, defat, and reheat the sauce and slice the meat; because the brisket will still be hot, there will be no need to put it back into the oven once the reheated sauce is poured over it.
